entries.title: Front-of-neck airway

sources.label: DAS 2015 (CICO)
sources.detail: Frerk C, Mitchell VS, McNarry AF, et al. Difficult Airway Society 2015 guidelines for management of unanticipated difficult intubation in adults. Br J Anaesth. 2015;115(6):827-848.
sources.basis: Landmark: Cricothyroid membrane lies between thyroid and cricoid cartilages — identify with the laryngeal handshake

sources.label: Gray's Anatomy 42e
sources.detail: Standring S, ed. Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice. 42nd ed. Elsevier; 2020.
sources.basis: Landmark: Thyroid isthmus overlies tracheal rings 2–4 — below the cricoid, not at the membrane

entries.title: Pelvic ring and binder position

sources.label: Bonner 2011 Binder
sources.detail: Bonner TJ, Eardley WG, Newell N, et al. Accurate placement of a pelvic binder improves reduction of unstable fractures of the pelvic ring. J Bone Joint Surg Br 2011;93:1524-8.
sources.basis: Landmark: Centre the binder over the greater trochanters, not the iliac crests — high placement reduces the fracture poorly

sources.label: Gray's Anatomy 42e
sources.detail: Standring S, ed. Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice. 42nd ed. Elsevier; 2020.
sources.basis: Landmark: Most pelvic fracture bleeding is venous, from the presacral and paravesical plexuses and fracture surfaces

entries.title: Obturator nerve and the bladder wall

sources.label: Gray's Anatomy 42e
sources.detail: Standring S, ed. Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice. 42nd ed. Elsevier; 2020.
sources.basis: Landmark: The obturator nerve (L2–L4) runs along the lateral pelvic wall, close to the inferolateral bladder wall, to the obturator canal

entries.credit: Custom labelled line diagram; simplified and not to scale.

entries.title: Prostate and fluid absorption in TURP

sources.label: Hahn 2006 Fluid Absorption
sources.detail: Hahn RG. Fluid absorption in endoscopic surgery. Br J Anaesth. 2006;96(1):8-20.
sources.basis: Landmark: Irrigating fluid enters the circulation through opened prostatic venous sinuses, and into the tissues if the capsule is perforated

entries.title: Femoral triangle

sources.label: Gray's Anatomy 42e
sources.detail: Standring S, ed. Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice. 42nd ed. Elsevier; 2020.
sources.basis: Landmark: Below the inguinal ligament the order from lateral to medial is femoral nerve, artery, vein, then the femoral canal

sources.label: 3SITES 2015
sources.detail: Parienti JJ et al. Intravascular complications of central venous catheterization by insertion site (3SITES). N Engl J Med. 2015;373(13):1220-1229.
sources.basis: Landmark: Femoral catheters carried a higher rate of infection and thrombosis than subclavian catheters in a large randomised trial

entries.title: Internal jugular vein

sources.label: Gray's Anatomy 42e
sources.detail: Standring S, ed. Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice. 42nd ed. Elsevier; 2020.
sources.basis: Landmark: The internal jugular vein lies in the carotid sheath, usually lateral to the carotid artery, beneath sternocleidomastoid

sources.label: NICE TA49
sources.detail: NICE. Guidance on the use of ultrasound locating devices for placing central venous catheters (TA49). 2002.
sources.basis: Landmark: Ultrasound guidance is recommended for internal jugular cannulation

entries.title: Abdominal aorta and clamp levels

sources.label: Gray's Anatomy 42e
sources.detail: Standring S, ed. Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice. 42nd ed. Elsevier; 2020.
sources.basis: Landmark: Coeliac trunk, superior mesenteric and renal arteries arise in sequence; most aneurysms are infrarenal

sources.label: BJA Educ AAA 2016
sources.detail: Spence S, Doyle J. Anaesthesia for elective open and endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair. BJA Education. 2016;16(11):373-378.
sources.basis: Landmark: Suprarenal clamping adds renal (and possibly visceral) ischaemia and a larger rise in afterload than infrarenal clamping

sources.label: Taterra 2019 Adamkiewicz
sources.detail: Taterra D, Skinningsrud B, Pękala PA, et al. Artery of Adamkiewicz: a meta-analysis of anatomical characteristics. Neuroradiology 2019;61:869-80.
sources.basis: Landmark: The artery of Adamkiewicz usually arises on the left between T8 and L1 — at risk in thoracoabdominal repair

entries.credit: Custom labelled line diagram; simplified and not to scale.
uncertainty: Adamkiewicz origin is variable and this depiction is simplified.

entries.title: Carotid bifurcation

sources.label: Gray's Anatomy 42e
sources.detail: Standring S, ed. Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice. 42nd ed. Elsevier; 2020.
sources.basis: Landmark: Common carotid divides at about C4 (upper border of thyroid cartilage); the carotid sinus baroreceptor sits at the bulb, supplied by IX

sources.label: Cunningham 2004 CEA Nerves
sources.detail: Cunningham EJ, Bond R, Mayberg MR, Warlow CP, Rothwell PM. Risk of persistent cranial nerve injury after carotid endarterectomy. J Neurosurg 2004;101:445-8.
sources.basis: Landmark: Hypoglossal, vagus (recurrent laryngeal) and marginal mandibular nerves are at risk; most injuries are transient

sources.label: GALA 2008
sources.detail: GALA Trial Collaborative Group. General anaesthesia versus local anaesthesia for carotid surgery (GALA): a multicentre, randomised controlled trial. Lancet. 2008;372(9656):2132-2142.
sources.basis: Landmark: GALA found no difference in stroke, MI or death between general and local anaesthesia
